data.title: French Unrest: Are we witnessing a new 'Yellow Vests' movement?
data.description:
It's been 18 days since we first reported on isolated cases of schools protests at a high school in Rennes in Brittany, in Caen in Normandy and Villeneueve d'Asque on the suburbs of Lille. The complaints were similar in theme, overloaded timetables, staffing problems, poor facilities. It spread to Saint Denis and Creteil on the outskirts of Paris days later, one interview with the students was sen 1.4 million times on TikTok. It gathered pace, and morphed into what we've seen throughout the week, hundreds of protests, some peaceful, some with deeply distressing scenes, beyond the make shift barricades, a school in Nantes set off fire, firefighters forced out of the vehicle in Marseille and the fire engine set alight, scroll your socials itt's hard to miss some of the uglier scenes, a female police officer being attacked on the ground as youths shouted kill her. Where is it heading, and what has it become? Urban violence says the government, accusing agitators linked to the hard left exploiting geenuine concerns for political ends ahead of the election. Which La France Insoumise denies saying they favour no violent means of action. 
 
Today in Spotlight, we discuss this with Jean Remi Girard, a teacher in Asnieres in the north of Paris, and the President of the National Union des Lycees and Colleges, covering education workers from primary schools to college, 7 until 18.

data.title: 'We have to close defence gaps urgently': EU Parliament Foreign Affairs Committee chief McAllister
data.description: We sit down with David McAllister, the chair of the European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee. data.title: Brazil: The craze for candidate merch ahead of elections

data.title: ‘People are deserting it’: why are London mansions struggling to sell?
data.description: For decades, the capital’s house prices raced ahead of the national average – but now they are falling in prime areas An elegant Georgian facade, a full-width balcony and an exclusive address in South Kensington just steps from the Natural History Museum and the V&A. Yet the listing price of this west London flat at Queen’s Gate Gardens has dropped by nearly £1m since last year, to £4.4m. It is far from an isolated case. A nearby house originally listed at £20m was slashed to £14m this year, says a local estate agent. In neighbouring Notting Hill, a stucco-fronted property that came to market two years ago at £16m is now being offered for less than £14m, they said. Continue reading...

data.title: Bangkok at breaking point as floods turn streets into stagnant lakes
data.description: With 40 dead and a disaster declared across all 50 city districts, experts warn extreme flooding will only worsen across south-east Asia Bangkok is used to absorbing the sudden afternoon downpours that inundate the city during the rainy season. Even streets in many central high-rise districts can briefly turn into rivers, with rats and cockroaches racing out of sewers and taking temporary refuge on trees and buildings as the subterranean world is flushed out. But every city has a breaking point, and this year rain fell so fast and so hard that whole neighbourhoods of the Thai capital have been transformed, not into rivers, but stagnant lakes. In parts of the city, roughly 300mm of rain – the equivalent of half a year of average rainfall in London – fell in about two days. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s not just about getting drunk!’ How Oktoberfest took over the UK
data.description: Bavaria’s boozy blowout has inspired dozens of British tributes, from Belfast to Beverley, Cardiff to Cambridge.  But what’s the attraction, other than the beer and the bratwurst? Under a sea of Bavarian bunting, vendors hand out steins of pilsner, dunkel and weissbier, alongside platters of bratwurst, pork knuckle and pretzels. The lederhosen-clad Bettesteiner Footstompers lead the cheering crowd in a boisterous oompah singalong: “Eins, zwei, g’suffa!” (“One, two, drink up!”) Foot-tapping, glass-clinking and swaying soon turn into dancing, and eventually a full-blown conga. The spirit of Oktoberfest is well and truly upon us – but Munich is more than 500 miles away. My friends and I are at Wünder Harbour in Folkestone, Kent, a homage to the German event. Wünder Harbour has been held since 2023, first over one weekend, and now four as its popularity has rocketed. It is just one of scores of Oktoberfest tributes all over the UK, from tiny bars to enormous marquees in pretty much every major city. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘An extraordinary hour’: the explosive play re-staging the biggest TV clash of the Aids era
data.description: A New York production brings Larry Kramer and Anthony Fauci’s 1993 debate to life in a masterclass of controlled fury On 30 November 1993, the Aids activist Larry Kramer and Anthony Fauci , director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, were arguing again. They argued a lot back then about the US government’s response, or lack thereof, to the Aids crisis. Fauci asserted institutional legitimacy. Kramer scolded that any institution presiding over a genocide doesn’t have any. Kramer wanted to untie Fauci’s hands from politics and bureaucracy; Fauci wanted to de-escalate Kramer’s vituperous hand-wringing. They also ribbed each other, allies as often as antagonists. On the night they appeared on C-Span, the buttoned-up not-for-profit cable channel better known for unfettered congressional coverage than for the verbal pyrotechnics of CNN’s Crossfire, or the revelations-as-entertainment approach to politics by Oprah and Donahue. But this night was different. Journalist Steve Scully spent the hour trying to moderate Kramer and Fauci as they attacked and amused each other: he redirected them back to his questions when passions erupted, and kept those questions to centrist concerns of, mostly, money. And in between all this he took he took calls from civilians whose empathy and expertise in Aids, let’s say, ranged wildly. It was an exhausting hour, which settled little. But it showed what just might happen when people yell at each other loudly enough so they can be heard, and also listen. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I thought, if I’m going to die, I’m going to write a book first’: Pachinko author Min Jin Lee
data.description: Her last novel sold 5m copies and was adapted into a hit series. Nearly 10 years on, the Korean-American author has written another epic. She discusses ambition and the diagnosis that inspired her to leave work and write Back in 1995, when she was in her mid-20s, Min Jin Lee quit her job as a corporate lawyer. As a teenager she had been diagnosed as a hepatitis B carrier and doctors told her she was highly likely to develop liver cancer in her 20s or 30s. “I thought, if I’m going to die, I’m going to write a book first,” the now 57-year-old Korean-American author says of her decision to turn her back on a regular pay cheque and healthcare. “I was told so many times that I was going to get sicker and sicker, that I’ve always felt that if I can get a really good book out then I’m done.” Lee, looking very much alive and well, is on a video call from her home in Harlem, New York, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves behind her. We are meeting to discuss the publication of her third novel, American Hagwon, the final part in what she calls her “Korean trilogy”, following Free Food for Millionaires in 2007 and her 2017 international bestseller, Pachinko , stylishly adapted for Apple TV in 2022. “Korean quartet!” she corrects me now. Thanks to experimental drugs, she is now so healthy she can commit to another book. “Before I turn 70, I should turn in my manuscript,” she jokes. “I’m writing the four books that I wanted to write and after that I’m going to take a long nap.” Continue reading...

data.title: The football horse that Andy Burnham rode in on is now bucking his vibe | Barney Ronay
data.description: PM’s contortions over the Manchester City verdicts have landed him with an early test of what he wants to stand for. Realpolitik, or real values? It’s coming for you. It’s coming for you. Oh Andy Burnham, the hugely problematic relationship between principle and realpolitik in post-cash Britain. It’s coming for you. We are going all in on football chat these days, aren’t we? Football populism, football blokeyness, the stylings of the football everyman. That was certainly the horse the prime minister rode in on a few months ago. And right now it’s a horse that’s still very much snorting around the cabinet room, and threatening to run right over the top of him. Also: fresh plot twists. Previous governments have been thrown into early-term crisis by things such as war, sex scandals and economic meltdown. But never, and historians will have time to pore over this in the coming decades, by the urgent need to overpay for Jack Grealish. “The ramifications of this are MASSIVE,” the man on the radio said on Thursday morning. And he was right. There are ramifications here. And the ramifications, well, Clive, they’re massive. In this case the man on the radio was discussing the United Kingdom’s multilayered geopolitical meltdown through the prism of whether this means Spurs are less or more likely to get relegated. And to be fair there are very few global events that can’t be better understood through a Spurs-in-crisis lens. Continue reading...

data.title: What do Britain’s death-penalty cheerleaders have to say about Christa Pike? | Maya Foa
data.description: Her harrowing botched execution is a reminder of why we must not even entertain the idea of restoring capital punishment Maya Foa is the CEO of the human rights charity Reprieve In recent months, there has been a resurgence of interest in the death penalty among rightwing politicians in the UK. The leader of Restore Britain, Rupert Lowe, has made a manifesto commitment to holding a legally binding referendum on bringing back capital punishment. The Reform MP Lee Anderson is also in favour of a referendum, arguing that the public would vote in favour of the death penalty. Such supporters of capital punishment in Britain point to polls such as this “ bombshell survey ” that supposedly showed 47% of students favoured bringing back the death penalty. data.title: It's true: this is my final column. You have exactly 24 hours to complain before my inbox self-destructs | Marina Hyde
data.description: Yes, after 25 years I’m signing off, and I’ve cherished every moment – especially storming the French embassy with a (toy) AK-47 Journalism 101 – a course I have yet to complete – dictates that if you have something salient to say you should get there fast. So right now, I should mention that this is my last ever column for the Guardian. I’ll level with you: I spent a long time wondering how to write it. At first, I thought it should be about all the things I’ve learned, purely because that would be a hell of a lot shorter than a column about all the things I keep failing to learn, no matter how many times I make the mistakes. For example: if you’ve got a good joke, you’d best put it in the intro. (Why is there literally no joke in this intro?) Or: remember that people love the piss-taking until it strays into the arena of something they like, when it suddenly becomes wholly unacceptable. Take the time I wrote: “Arguing on the internet is like playing real tennis: even if you win, you’re still a twat ”. This prompted an immediate missive from a member of the Cambridge University real tennis club, which appeared on the letters page under the headline “ Real tennis has been served badly by this unfair slur ” and began: “Like many Guardian readers, I have thoroughly enjoyed and always look forward to reading Marina Hyde’s witty and caustic commentaries on the world about us. However …” Incidentally, I told this story at one book tour event, and then at the signing afterwards, a lovely young lady came up to get a book dedicated to her father, Jeremy. And of course, she said: “I should probably mention, he’s the guy who wrote in from the Cambridge University real tennis club.” Truly, the circle of life. To Jeremy, and the many other Jeremies who have written in over the years, let me just say: we all know the real twats are rackets players. Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnist She’s been making sense of the madness for the last 25 years: celebrate the end of an era with Marina Hyde’s final column collection, What a Time to Be Alive! To support the Guardian, order your signed copy at guardianbookshop.com . Delivery charges may apply Continue reading...

At first, I thought it should be about all the things I’ve learned, purely because that would be a hell of a lot shorter than a column about all the things I keep failing to learn, no matter how many times I make the mistakes. For example: if you’ve got a good joke, you’d best put it in the intro. (Why is there literally no joke in this intro?) Or: remember that people love the piss-taking until it strays into the arena of something they like, when it suddenly becomes wholly unacceptable. Take the time I wrote: “Arguing on the internet is like playing real tennis: even if you win, you’re still a twat ”. This prompted an immediate missive from a member of the Cambridge University real tennis club, which appeared on the letters page under the headline “ Real tennis has been served badly by this unfair slur ” and began: “Like many Guardian readers, I have thoroughly enjoyed and always look forward to reading Marina Hyde’s witty and caustic commentaries on the world about us. However …” Incidentally, I told this story at one book tour event, and then at the signing afterwards, a lovely young lady came up to get a book dedicated to her father, Jeremy. And of course, she said: “I should probably mention, he’s the guy who wrote in from the Cambridge University real tennis club.” Truly, the circle of life. To Jeremy, and the many other Jeremies who have written in over the years, let me just say: we all know the real twats are rackets players. Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnist She’s been making sense of the madness for the last 25 years: celebrate the end of an era with Marina Hyde’s final column collection, What a Time to Be Alive! data.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
data.description: A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures ; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport. For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”. As chancellor, Rachel Reeves claimed that a third runway at Heathrow would add 0.43% to GDP , figures we later discovered came from a report commissioned by the airport. The transport department’s own analysis concluded that the real addition to GDP would be between 0.03% and 0.05%: eight to 14 times less. Against this, it weighed the social and environmental costs of the project, to reveal a massive net loss. It found that a third runway would cause major harm to the health and wellbeing of up to 3 million local people . George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: How best to punish City? Restitution over retribution, then hand club to the fans | Jonathan Liew
data.description: There are no real precedents and emotions are still raw, but good can come from this mess if ownership models change A 17-year transfer embargo. Replay the entire era with all the original players. Restore the 2009 squad and force them to mount a title challenge with Stephen Ireland, Martin Petrov and Richard Dunne. Force Ferran Soriano to drive a parade bus backwards through Manchester, once for every major trophy won. Ban the Poznan, or at least make City fans do it facing forwards. Yes, in the week since it emerged that Manchester City have been found guilty of all the financial charges laid against them by the Premier League, a great and cathartic silliness has begun to stalk the land. The Sainsbury’s account on Instagram posting a picture that reads “114 unexpected items in the bagging area”. The relentless trolling from Domino’s Pizza, which claims to have “irrefutable evidence that pineapple is the best pizza topping”. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Barack Obama’s new podcast: all the president’s books | Editorial
data.description: From Oprah Winfrey to Dua Lipa, there is no shortage of celebrity literary champions. But the former US leader is in a class of his own At the Labour party conference Andy Burnham revealed that Hamlet , Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness and Tony Harrison’s poem V are his favourite works of literature. The UK’s first prime minister with an English literature degree was not the only political figure sharing his book choices last week. Barack Obama, the US’s most literary president since Abraham Lincoln, launched a new podcast in which he discusses six books that shaped him with writer friends. First up was the actor – and recently turned short story writer – Tom Hanks on Marilynne Robinson’s Gilead , a meditation on faith, fatherhood and forgiveness in the form of a letter written by a 76-year-old pastor to his son. It was an unabashedly highbrow start. With the exception of John le Carré’s cold war classic Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, Mr Obama’s selections are American: Toni Morrison’s Song of Solomon, Cormac McCarthy’s All the Pretty Horses, James Baldwin’s essays The Fire Next Time and Robert Penn Warren’s All the King’s Men. Questions of democracy, race, power and violence are all here. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Hawaii’s centuries-old sea arch collapses into Pacific after series of rough storms
data.description: Hōlei sea arch, formed 550 years ago by erosion from ocean waves, no longer standing, National Park Service confirms A famed centuries-old sea arch on Hawaii’s remote and rugged coastline has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean, the National Park Service confirmed on Friday, following a stretch of rough storms in the region in recent weeks. The beloved landmark, Hōlei sea arch, stood at around 90ft high for over half a millennium in Hawaii’s Volcanoes national park, located on the dramatic southern coast of the Big Island. It was naturally formed around 550 years ago due to differential erosion by ocean waves. Continue reading...

data.title: The American dream remains elusive in the valley that inspired East of Eden
data.description: John Steinbeck’s hometown of Salinas is the least affordable city in the US for the middle class, a recent Brookings Institution analysis found Nestled between two mountain ranges at the crook of central California’s coastline sits a valley known as the “salad bowl of the world”. Farm workers stoop over neatly lined rows of crops off Highway 101 to harvest more than half of the nation’s supply of lettuce and nearly a third of its strawberries. The soil here is so rich that author John Steinbeck made the Salinas valley the promised land in his literary depictions of people chasing the American dream: immigrants, farm workers, westward-moving hopefuls, hungering for a better life. data.description: New York film festival: The actor stumbles through Tony Gilroy’s forgettable film marred by stylistic gimmicks Tony Gilroy has built a sturdy career as the director of the Bourne films and show runner of the popular Star Wars spin-off Andor . He directed Tilda Swinton all the way to an Oscar for her remarkable performance in the legal potboiler Michael Clayton. As the first feature film he has directed since 2012’s The Bourne Legacy , the classical music drama Behemoth! promised to be an intriguing return from a master of threading the needle between slick action and deeply felt drama. His new film comes with a score from nine A-list composers who have banded together and called themselves The Behemoth! Collective, a stacked cast and a womanizing central character who looks phenomenal in a tux: “ Tár for straight men”, as a friend of mine put it. Continue reading...

data.title: Get Jiro: Anthony Bourdain’s ultraviolent sushi chef makes for wild, pulpy television
data.description: A love of food and a taste for bloodthirsty action collide as a very angry chef gets caught up in a brutal turf war between warring restaurants in LA Has foodie culture gone too far? It’s a truism that to get to a lasagne recipe now, you have to wade through an essay about someone’s childhood in Tuscany. We talk about food sentimentally, consume TV about it fetishistically, slavering over slow-motion shots of chopped pepper falling on to stainless steel. We enjoy judging the food of others. We talk about the provenance of our ingredients with a kind of purity fixation. It strikes me that there’s a totalitarianism to it. So it was bracing to watch Get Jiro (from Sunday 4 October, HBO Max), an adult animation that pairs a love of food with a taste for ultraviolence. It’s the story of a sushi chef, caught up in a bloodthirsty turf war between warring restaurants. It is set in a dystopian near-future Los Angeles, in which all human desires “including companionship, travel and sex, can be experienced … virtually”. (The episodes I’ve seen don’t go into this, explaining for example how chiropody could be experienced virtually, but that’s beside the point.) Continue reading...

data.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall review – Paul Thomas Anderson’s sumptuous recording is an immediate classic
data.description: New York Film Festival: The Geese frontman mesmerizes in a concert film that is both swoony and austere One night last December, weary from a busy week and the impending doom of winter, I hurried into Carnegie Hall to witness Cameron Winter. The Geese frontman was marking the end of a breakout year with a series of rapturously received solo acoustic shows, drawing the penitent for whom the 23-year-old’s primordial voice struck some kind of destabilizing natural frequency. I had bought the ticket months earlier, after being hypnotized by Winter’s beguiling debut solo album, Heavy Metal, and sat transfixed in the rafters, far from the Brooklynite’s lanky, stygian presence before a single piano. So far, in fact, that I assumed the maybe-camera that came on stage at one point was a bit, perhaps a jab at our incessant need to film things from a very deadpan celebrity whose only non-music interlude that evening was to wordlessly stand, stretch and mockingly fight with the stage door, as if trying to escape his own momentous show. I emerged from the event teary, charged by what felt like a communion across time, and confused by a friend’s text: “can’t wait for the cameron winter PTA doc”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s radical to release a film called Girls Like Girls in this climate’: hitmaker turned director Hayley Kiyoko on sexuality, safety and becoming ‘Lesbian Jesus’
data.description: The singer’s hit 2015 single Girls Like Girls was her breakthrough moment and also the first time she felt confident in her sexuality. Now she has directed a film based on the song – a love letter to her 17-year-old self A lot of Hayley Kiyoko’s teenage summers were spent waiting, bored and pining, as she sat at the computer willing her crush to message her back on AOL instant messenger. Like Coley, the 17-year-old protagonist of Girls Like Girls, the film the pop star has co-written and directed, Kiyoko fell hard for a girl who “put me through my own heartbreak and haunted me for a long time”, she says. Although the 35-year-old singer became known by fans as “lesbian Jesus” following the release of her breakthrough single Girls Like Girls in 2015 (the film is an extended version of the story first told in the song’s music video), feeling comfortable in her sexuality didn’t actually come until after its release. Her gay identity was, at the time, the topic she was “the most scared of writing about”, and the song’s confident refrain “Girls like girls like boys do, nothing new” came from wanting to “manifest feeling confident”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s rational to fear the music industry’: Grouper’s Liz Harris on virality, streaming scammers and her ‘restorative’ dream-pop trio
data.description: When a rarity blew up on TikTok, the solitary ambient artist had fraudsters trying to steal her royalties. It reinforced her DIY mentality – until reforming her band Helen reminded her of the beauty of collaboration In mid-September, I watched as Liz Harris soundchecked to 1,500 empty seats at midtown Manhattan’s historic Town Hall theatre. Soon each plush red chair would be filled for the second of two sold-out nights, but this ornate seclusion felt oddly perfect. It is fair to infer that most of her concertgoers generally listen to the uncanny experimental music she makes as Grouper alone, just as she creates it. Harris started Grouper in 2005 in the DIY noise warehouses of Oakland, California. At 46, she now lives farther north, in coastal Astoria, Oregon, where she creates densely tessellated visual art and spare, lucid albums that have made her a titan of modern ambient music. Painfully beautiful and often inscrutable, hers is a sonic language all its own, creating thickets of sound using little more than guitar or piano, voice and space; her angelic and alien songs have influenced artists as disparate as Phoebe Bridgers and Mk.gee , and been sampled by Lil B and 100 Gecs. It is intensely solitary work, often characterised as sad but full of profound relief. “Like a bloodletting,” Harris offers. Continue reading...

data.title: Add to playlist: the beautiful, breakneck chaos of Heavensouls and the week’s best new tracks
data.description: His hyperactive stylistic shifts and high-speed rhythms have a delirious, head-spinning beauty of their own From Biafra, Nigeria/Texas, USA Recommended if you like Los Thuthanaka, Jpegmafia, DJ Sabrina the Teenage DJ Up next Album Cantu of the Sower released via NTS Recordings on 7 October Many listeners might find blown-out noise, hyperactive stylistic shifts and breakneck rhythms a hellish prospect, and fair enough. But for a certain stripe of sensory freak, such swarming intensity can tip over into a state of heady relaxation. The ultra-prolific Heavensouls’ latest project scratches that itch: the six songs on Cantu of the Sower glitter like rich seams of rare crystal, billowing from arcade glitter to compression-straining bass, sprite-like playfulness to warm, rushing brass. Languid trumpet lines float around trash-compactor crunch; sugary breakbeats reach tweaky maximalist peaks. I don’t know about you, but I could bathe in it. Continue reading...

data.title: The best recent poetry – review roundup
data.description: Have It by John Cooper Clarke; The Dodo Stories by Mary Mulholland; Red River Valley by Ian McMillan;  Some Sacred Harbour by Roger Robinson; Otherwhere by Carolyn Forché Have It by John Cooper Clarke (Picador, £16.99) The latest collection from the original “people’s poet” displays his characteristic swagger, delivered with a distinctively northern humour. Merging blistering social satire and brash wit, Cooper Clarke irreverently tackles themes from the ridiculous to the sublime, including the malaise of contemporary urban life, the erosion of nature and the environment, money and the prospect of a cashless society, death and ageing, fascism, bachelorhood, popular culture and the NHS. His punk rock values caustically underpin the collection: “Me and my shrinking crowd / Each under our own personal cloud”; “We wish you no serious harm/ However, everybody sucks but us”. There’s heavy use of doggerel and jokes as he stridently proclaims his passion for writing. “It’s a meaningless job but someone’s got to do it / Thank God it’s me”. Overall, Cooper Clarke’s consummate performance skills in playing to the crowd demand applause as he advocates for the “blood royal of the working class”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Starchitects go home’: what’s the truth behind Albania’s astonishing building boom?
data.description: Sixty top architecture firms from around the world have mooted 500 eye-catching projects across Albania, sparking fury and protests. Now they’re being celebrated in an 800-page tome that some are calling ‘a smoking gun’ Last autumn, I was sitting with a prominent architect in New York, when their phone wouldn’t stop buzzing. They finally checked the messages and chuckled. “Oh, the Albanian Architecture Army chat is blowing up again,” they said. “It looks like Edi has some new projects for us.” Edi was Edi Rama, the prime minister of Albania since 2013, who has been presiding over the rapid transformation of the former communist country with a fleet of glamorous building projects. There are twisting towers in Tirana, along with prize-winning public spaces , striking coastal resorts, and many more dazzling visions on the way – all now brought together in a hefty new book, The Albanian Files . Continue reading...

data.title: Henry Harris’s recipe for vegetarian endive au gratin
data.description: A worthy, meat-free version of the best comfort dish ever, this French classic is best served with a chilled red and a crisp salad This is the best comfort dish on planet Earth. Cauliflower cheese held that title when I was a child, but I still remember the first time I ate this gratin, made by Simon Hopkinson at his restaurant Hilaire in London, and wanting to take it away and eat it in a quiet corner. Endive when braised well retains a gentle bitterness that contrasts beautifully with a cheese-heavy bechamel. This dish is traditionally made with comté and with each endive wrapped in a slice of cooked ham, but some dark, crisp-fried mushrooms and emmental serve very well as good, savoury vegetarian alternatives. Henry Harris is chef/co-owner of Bouchon Racine , London EC1. His book, The Racine Effect, is published by Quadrille at £40. To order a copy for £36, go to guardianbookshop.com Continue reading...

data.title: Tim Dowling: nobody’s laughing – is the joke on me?
data.description: By over-committing to the bit, I’m in danger of becoming the very thing that I mock There was a kid in my year in high school named Jimmy Tremarelli. We were in a couple of the same classes, and also had occasion to pass each other in the hall between bells about three times a day. Whenever we did Jimmy would nod and say, “Dr Dowling”, and I would say, “Dr Tremarelli”. And then we’d carry on in opposite directions. Over the years the pretence became gradually more elaborate. Sometimes Jim would steal up alongside me at the end of class, cupping my elbow in the palm of his hand. Continue reading...

data.title: The simple secrets behind great ramen
data.description: You need five things: broth, flavour-giving tare, noodles, fat and toppings. And it’s the toppings that make it really special. Here are five versions, from a Toyko classic to a new Cardiff cult hit Watch our guide to the UK’s best ramen renegades in Feed with Jimi Famurewa At its simplest, ramen is the balance of five elements: broth, tare (secret seasoning sauce), noodles, fat and toppings. If you understand that, this seemingly cryptic and complex corner of Japanese food culture opens right up. The first four take time, but if you pick up a shop-bought stock and some decent noodles, I won’t tell anyone. But the toppings are where the real payoff is: the fastest way to turn a midweek nothing into something worth showing off. A universal note Spring onions should be used to top every bowl (finely diced white onion will work as a backup). Where there’s a broth, aim for 300ml, and where dashi is mentioned, instant is fine – unless you’re vegan, in which case steep 20g each of kombu and dried shiitake in one litre of cold water overnight, and keep the mushrooms for the soboro. Noodle portions are 130g unless stated otherwise, and any specialist items should be available online or at your local Asian supermarket. Continue reading...

data.title: Brimful of personality: the rise of fashion’s ‘silly little hats’
data.description: From pillboxes and boaters to bicornes and buckets, characterful hats are making their way from the catwalk to the high street “Here goes – an order for a million hats,” wrote Jackie Kennedy to Bergdorf Goodman before moving into the White House in the early 1960s. It’s a line that could have been uttered by any number of people working in fashion today, because the hat – and not just the ubiquitous baseball cap – has been enjoying a very characterful resurgence. This season at the turbo-high-end brand Loro Piana, whose clothes are beloved by tech bros and Kendall Roy, almost every model was wearing a hat . At Thom Browne, straw boaters came shrouded in colourful mesh. At Chloé there were see-through hats to match see-through trenchcoats and white sailor hats atop all-white outfits. Courrège’s hats were space-age, Burberry had big buckets, Bottega Veneta had hats brimming with charisma. Continue reading...

data.title: Daniel Roseberry adds ‘aerodynamic‘ edge to Schiaparelli’s surrealist glamour at Paris show
data.description: American in Paris showcases new simplicity with stretch cocktail frocks, but there’s still plenty of gold-foiled nipples and peekaboo fabrics to wow the frow In a world of mega brands, the house of Schiaparelli is small but perfectly formed. There are only 10 points of sale worldwide where Schiaparelli clothes can be bought. The size of the business has risen from $6m in 2020 to around $100m today, but Schiaparelli is still small fry compared with other names on the Paris catwalks. However, the Schiaparelli name punches above its weight. An exhibition at London’s V&A museum this year made a strong case for its founder, Elsa Schiaparelli, who collaborated with Salvador Dali and Jean Cocteau, as a creative force in the surrealism movement of the 1930s. data.title: They’re delicious, popular and versatile – but how healthy are berries?
data.description: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits. Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber. Research shows that, depending on the type, berries support cardiovascular health , may boost gut health and fight inflammation and show promise as part of a “healthy dietary strategy for diabetes prevention and management”, to quote researchers . Meta-analyses also link compounds in berries with improved cognitive health. Continue reading...

data.title: Feeling wired? The truth about ‘nervous system resets’
data.description: The internet is full of warnings about our ‘dysregulated’ nervous systems. But, experts say, you don’t need to reset yours – you might just need to make it more flexible. Here’s how (and no, you don’t need an acupressure mat) Whether it’s tapping the side of your hand or standing on a vibrating plate, suggestions on how to “reset” your nervous system are saturating the internet. Cold water plunges, humming, gargling, yawning and spiky acupressure mats are all being touted as ways to help us “regulate” and return to calm. If you’re still talking about feeling “stressed”, you’re behind the times; now, says the internet, you are “dysregulated”. The nervous system is an integral part of being human. “It’s essentially the body’s communication and control network,” says Dr Serena Lai, consultant psychiatrist and associate medical director at London Psychiatry Clinic. “Made up of the brain and spinal cord, it communicates with the entire body through nerves, helping us to sense what is happening around and inside us. When we have that information, we can process it and coordinate a response.” Continue reading...

data.title: In the footsteps of Wales’s heroic rebel prince: hiking Glyndŵr’s Way
data.description: As Michael Sheen prepares to bring Owain Glyndŵr to life on stage, our writer walks the peaceful national trail named after the last Welsh Prince of Wales Between the treetops, I can see the towers of a distant mist-shrouded castle. Is it possible I could make contact with the spirit of the great Welsh hero Owain Glyndŵr so soon, at the very start of our hike? We are not even on the actual trail of Glyndŵr’s Way . I’ve had to make a detour to find accommodation that takes dogs, as Stevie the terrier is with me. The Castle Inn at Knucklas is a mile off the route, and two miles or so from the pretty border town of Knighton – where the 135-mile (217km) Glyndŵr’s Way officially begins. The towers slide away behind trees and a railway viaduct emerges. The medieval castle ruins, it turns out, are believed to have been plundered to build the viaduct in the 1860s, and the builders dropped in a couple of crenelated towers to honour the origins of the stone. I fear this may be an early omen: the spirit of Glyndŵr will be as elusive as the man himself was in his lifetime. Continue reading...

data.title: 658 unmarked graves found at two remote Australian cemeteries after specialist search
data.description: A groundbreaking project has identified 658 previously unmarked graves at the White Cliffs and Menindee cemeteries in Australia. Utilizing advanced non-invasive scanning techniques, Hunter Geophysics successfully located these burial sites, ensuring no disturbance to the ground. This initiative aims to enhance cemetery management and heritage conservation, with plans for memorialization at White Cliffs for those honored. Such efforts emphasize the crucial need to preserve local history and cemetery documentation.

data.title: Que país queremos construir?
data.description: Estamos a algumas horas de mais uma eleição decisiva. Por isso esta coluna é para que possamos refletir: que país queremos construir? Porque votar não é apenas escolher quem ocupará um cargo público. É decidir quem terá poder para definir o destino das nossas florestas, dos nossos rios, dos territórios indígenas, das mulheres, das crianças, das populações tradicionais e de milhões de pessoas que dependem diretamente das políticas públicas para viver com dignidade. Nestas eleições, não votaremos apenas para presidente. Também escolheremos governadores, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais ou distritais. São seis escolhas que, juntas, definirão a correlação de forças que governará o país nos próximos anos. Por isso é tão importante que sejamos conscientes. E consciência significa olhar para a história, para as posições públicas, para os projetos apresentados e, sobretudo, para aquilo que cada candidatura representa. Quando falamos de meio ambiente, falamos de água, comida, clima, saúde, cidades, agricultura, economia e vida. Quando falamos de povos indígenas, não falamos apenas de uma parcela da população. Estamos falando de povos que protegem territórios fundamentais para a biodiversidade, para as águas e para o equilíbrio climático, além de defenderem modos de vida e conhecimentos milenares. O que esperar de gente que pensa na linha de que a a cavalaria brasileira não foi tão eficiente quanto a americana porque não exterminou os indígenas? Outra questão importante: o que acontecerá no Congresso? Não basta escolher um presidente e imaginar que ele resolverá tudo. Senadores e deputados têm enorme poder para aprovar ou barrar leis, definir o Orçamento, alterar políticas públicas, fiscalizar o Executivo e modificar a legislação ambiental e os marcos que protegem direitos. É por isso que precisamos olhar para toda a composição do poder. Precisamos escolher representantes que compreendam que proteger uma terra indígena não é proteger apenas uma área no mapa. Precisamos de representantes que compreendam que política ambiental não pode ser tratada como obstáculo ao desenvolvimento. Precisamos de representantes que compreendam que direitos humanos não são privilégios. E precisamos, sobretudo, recuperar a capacidade de enxergar as consequências de nossas escolhas para além dos próximos quatro anos. Porque quem ocupa o Congresso decide sobre leis que podem durar décadas. Quem ocupa o Executivo define prioridades que podem transformar territórios inteiros. E quem chega ao poder também ajuda a definir aquilo que passa a ser considerado aceitável no debate público. O voto é individual. A responsabilidade por ele também. Cada pessoa fará suas próprias escolhas diante da urna. Mas essas escolhas terão consequências coletivas. A floresta não vota. O rio não vota. A onça não vota. As crianças que ainda não nasceram não votam. Uma eleição não define apenas os governantes. Define quais ideias terão poder. E algumas ideias, quando chegam ao poder, podem proteger a vida. Outras podem colocar a própria vida em risco. Leia mais (10/02/2026 - 23h47)

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Hur ska poliser hjälpa andra när de inte får rätt stöd?”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Poliser ska stå stadigt när de möter våld, dödsfall och barn som far illa – när de befinner sig mitt i människors värsta upplevelser. Men om de ska orka ett helt yrkesliv krävs mer än de insatser som finns i dag, de måste få långsiktigt stöd för sin mentala hälsa, skriver Mehdi Ghazinour, professor i polisvetenskap och Katharina von Sydow, ordförande i Polisförbundet.

data.title: Valskandal skakar Indien – 130 miljoner väljare strukna från röstlängden

data.title: Stockholm väntar med beslut om extern utredning om valet i Järva
data.description: På fredagen träffades kommunstyrelsen i Stockholm för ett extrainsatt möte med anledning av misstänkt valfusk i Järva. Moderaternas krav på att tillsätta en omedelbar extern utredning om saken fick inget gehör. Karin Wanngård (S) säger att förslagen måste beredas först. Statsvetaren Erik Wångman har svårt att se varför frågan skulle undgå beredning.

data.title: 78-årings bank-id spärrat efter bedrägeri – gick inte att överklaga

data.title: Skolelever först i Förbifartens tunnlar – över 30 000 löpare väntas på lördagen
data.description: Förbifarten, som ska gå från Kungens kurva till Häggvik, öppnar sin första etapp under hösten, fyra år innan hela motorvägsleden ska stå klar. Inför öppningen anordnar Marathongruppen ett motionslopp – men de första att beträda den nya vägen blev skolelever från Stockholm, Sollentuna och Järfälla. – Jag kände mig som en jätteviktig person, säger en av eleverna.

data.title: Trafikverkets utmaning – få bort den 100 ton tunga lastbilen från bron
data.description: En pontonfärja ska ersätta den skadade bron i Strömsund. För kommuninvånarna är det en enorm lättnad. För Trafikverket kvarstår den stora utmaningen – att få bort den 100 ton tunga lastbil som står kvar på den skadade Strömsundsbron. – Så länge den är kvar på bron kan vi inte ta reda på vad som gått sönder, varför det är trasigt eller hur vi ska åtgärda det, säger Peter Jonsson, presstalesperson på Trafikverket.

data.title: Musici en zussen Luna en Donna van Leeuwen organiseren Kinder Klimaat Concert Dag: ‘Met muziek kun je de emotie bereiken – voor de toekomst van een leefbare planeet’
data.description: Via muziek willen de zussen Luna (23) en Donna (20) van Leeuwen emoties losmaken rond het thema klimaat. Op 11 oktober organiseren de jonge musici de eerste Klimaat Concert Dag. Aan de hand van de vier seizoenen willen ze het publiek informeren, maar vooral laten voelen wat klimaatverandering betekent voor de jongste generatie en de planeet.

data.title: Een duurzame wereld heeft niet minder energie nodig, maar méér

data.title: Prognoza długoterminowa pokazuje zwrot w pogodzie. Czekają nas fale zimna i śnieg
data.description: Przed nami słoneczny i ciepły weekend w większości kraju. Warto wykorzystać sprzyjające warunki, ponieważ taka aura wkrótce się skończy. Długoterminowe prognozy mówią o nadchodzącym załamaniu pogody. Już pod koniec przyszłego tygodnia czeka nas duże ochłodzenie i opady deszczu. Gdzieniegdzie pojawią się nawet przymrozki i śnieg.

data.title: Odkryli strumień czarnej dziury skierowany prosto w Ziemię. „Krył się na widoku”
data.description: Astronomowie odkryli w naszej galaktyce obiekt, którego istnienie sugerowano od dawna, jednak nigdy nie udało się znaleźć na to dowodu. To mikroblazar w Drodze Mlecznej, czyli stosunkowo niewielka czarna dziura emitująca strumienie gorącej plazmy (dżety) poruszające się z bardzo dużą prędkością. Jeden z tych strumieni skierowany jest w stronę Ziemi.

data.title: Macecha s přehlíženou mocí. Brazilské volby může rozhodnout bývalá první dáma
data.description: Brazilské prezidentské volby jsou především soubojem dvou mužů, prezidenta Luize Inácia Luly da Silva a Flávia Bolsonara, syna exprezidenta Jaira Bolsonara. Jejich výsledek ale může nakonec rozhodnout někdo jiný – Fláviova macecha Michelle Bolsonarová, která má velké slovo u části ženského voličstva. Její vztahy s nevlastním synem přitom nejsou ideální a ukazují na dysfunkčnost rodinného klanu.

data.title: Peklo na Dněpru. Rusko útokem na další most trhá ještě víc Kyjev na kusy
data.description: Kyjev čelí nové, systematické vlně ruských vzdušných úderů, které se poprvé od začátku invaze zaměřily na paralyzování klíčových dopravních tepen přes řeku Dněpr. Zatímco doposud Rusko útočilo především na energetickou síť, současná strategie míří na samotný pohyb ve městě. V sobotu byl zasažen Severní most přes řeku Dněpr, oznámil starosta ukrajinské metropole Vitalij Kličko.

data.title: Lunetic si zopakoval třicetiny. Tentokrát i s Martinem Kociánem, hala z něj šílela
data.description: „Rádi slavíme,“ vysvětlil Vašek Jelínek s úsměvem druhou oslavu třicetin skupiny Lunetic. Na té loňské chyběl zakládající člen Martin Kocián, takže byl důvod dát si repete. Návrat v pravém slova smyslu se ovšem nekonal a některé fanoušky to zklamalo. S návštěvou Kata z Prago Union, skupinou Holki a Terezou Pergnerovou nicméně dostala vyprodaná hala O2 universum dávku nostalgie, pro kterou si přišla.

data.title: Z letních teplot rovnou pod deštník. V který den vtrhne do Česka prudký zlom
data.description: Slunečné dny a nadprůměrné teploty dostaly jasné datum skoro nevratného konce. data.title: Kopilot z letu Flydubai měl v domovské zemi zákaz létání. Kvůli extremismu
data.description: Pilot, který se pokusil o havárii letu Flydubai se 182 lidmi na palubě, měl v rodném Ománu zákaz létat, uvádí zdroj agentury AP a zdroje deníku The Wall Street Journal (WSJ). Existovaly obavy, že muž přejal extremistické názory. Později ho zaměstnala letecká společnost se sídlem ve Spojených arabských emirátech. Zatím není jasné, do jaké míry ho nový zaměstnavatel prověřoval.

Existovaly obavy, že muž přejal extremistické názory. Později ho zaměstnala letecká společnost se sídlem ve Spojených arabských emirátech. Zatím není jasné, do jaké míry ho nový zaměstnavatel prověřoval.

data.title: Vyjít s výplatou je problém. Většině na konci měsíce mnoho nezbude, říká průzkum
data.description: Stále více lidí má potíže vyjít s penězi. Alespoň dvacet procent z výplaty, případně i více, zbude na konci měsíce jen 43 procentům Čechů. Ještě loni to přitom bylo 52 procent, uvádí průzkum společnosti Provident Financial.

data.title: Zelená na přání. Plzeň jako první v ČR testuje chytré semafory pro hasiče
data.description: Hasiči v Plzni jako první v republice testují novou technologii, která jim při jízdě k zásahům s předstihem uvolňuje průjezd křižovatkami řízenými semafory. Laicky řečeno, vybraných 10 křižovatek je nově vybaveno zařízeními, která zachytí informace z palubních jednotek v hasičských autech a s předstihem se semafory ze všech směrů rozsvítí tak, aby hasiči projeli bez zdržení a co nejbezpečněji.

data.title: Chceme nakopnout stavbu městských bytů, říká lídr libereckých Pirátů
data.description: Liberečtí Piráti se do podzimních voleb spojili s opozičním uskupením Liberec otevřený lidem, jejich lídrem je čtyřicetiletý Jan Hruška. Stávající zastupitel a radní přibližuje, jak chce zajistit obyvatelům Liberce dostupné bydlení nebo jak krajské město učiní bezpečnějším. Prozrazuje také, co a proč závidí sousednímu Jablonci nad Nisou.

data.title: Bydlení je největší výzva, říká lídr Rychtecký. Žijeme Pardubice chystá přes 400 bytů
data.description: Už dvanáct let je náměstkem primátora. A letos chce svou pozici ještě posílit. Sdružení Žijeme Pardubice, jehož hlavní tváří je Jakub Rychtecký, totiž na kandidátku přibralo i politiky z dalších místních spolků, které před čtyřmi lety kandidovaly jako Společně pro Pardubice. „Spojuje nás to, že se známe z práce pro Pardubice a u řady věcí jsme už v minulosti dokázali spolupracovat. Jsme alternativou klasických politických stran,“ tvrdí Jakub Rychtecký, dvaačtyřicetiletý náměstek primátora.

data.title: „Přibyla mi hroší kůže.“ Primátorka Hradce Springerová chce tlačit velké projekty
data.description: V listopadu to budou čtyři roky, kdy si Hradec Králové poprvé v historii zvolil do svého čela ženu. Primátorka Pavlína Springerová se svým Hradeckým demokratickým klubem (HDK) sice volby nevyhrála, přesto dokázala poskládat vládnoucí koalici bez vítěze a dovést mandát do cíle. Primátorka věří, že jde o dočasný cíl a že po říjnových volbách dostane opět příležitost složit vedení.

data.title: Každý chce parkovací domy a víc bytů, ale ne ve své ulici, říká olomoucká lídryně ANO
data.description: Hnutí ANO drží v Olomouci post primátora od roku 2018 a chce v tom pokračovat i nadále, tentokrát s primátorkou Miroslavou Ferancovou. Ta vidí cestu k dalšímu rozvoji v hledání kompromisu mezi různými požadavky. „Každý chce parkovací domy a více bytů, ale ne ve své ulici. Hodně musíte vyvažovat zájmy jednotlivých skupin obyvatel,“ říká Ferancová.

data.title: Vězněného exposlance Wolfa čeká další soud. A patrně i předčasné propuštění
data.description: Bývalý poslanec za ČSSD Petr Wolf z Ostravy, který si od loňského podzimu odpykává v litoměřické věznici šestiletý trest odnětí svobody, chce požádat o předčasné propuštění. Nyní ho ale čeká další soud za to, že po pravomocném odsouzení za dotační podvod nenastoupil v roce 2012 do vězení. Později se ukázalo, že uprchl do Paraguaye. Odtamtud se vrátil s policejní eskortou před rokem.

data.title: Českým mlékárnám ujíždí vlak. Chybí cottage i skyry, tvrdí obchodníci
data.description: Tuzemské mlékárny neumějí zareagovat na změny spotřebitelského chování, na trhu chybějí cottage sýry, skyry, řecké jogurty nebo tvarohy z domácí produkce. Prakticky tak znějí závěry analýzy z pera Svazu obchodu a cestovního ruchu, tedy od zástupců obchodních řetězců. Podobně je na tom český trh i s mléčnými biovýrobky.

data.title: Dobré jídlo nemusí být nutně bio a eko. Pulty dobývá další díl kuchařských bichlí
data.description: Svačinkovou bichli, se kterou před šesti lety prorazila foodblogerka Pavlína Mähringová se svým týmem, postupně doplnily další kuchařky či komiks pro děti. Nyní autorka spustila předprodej Snídaňové bichle, která má proti předchozím titulům menší formát a sto receptů. „Vedle tištěných knih rozvíjíme také online aplikaci a chystáme pomocnici Aibi využívající umělou inteligenci,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iDNES. cz.

data.title: Na ilegální tuningový sraz v Praze dorazila tisícovka aut. V sobotu zamíří do Brna
data.description: Na ilegálním tuningovém srazu na parkovišti u hypermarketu Globus v pražských Čakovicích se podle odhadu policie sjelo až 1000 aut a 2500 lidí. Policie nezaznamenala žádné zásadní problémy. Na místě zajišťovala bezpečnost a případné přestupky bude řešit, řekl pražský policejní mluvčí Jan Daněk.  Akce v Čakovicích komplikovala provoz aut i veřejné dopravy.

data.title: Američanka po nezdařené popravě zůstává v bezvědomí a na přístrojích
data.description: Američanka Christa Pikeová, která skončila v nemocnici po nezdařené středeční popravě smrtící injekcí v Tennessee, zůstává v bezvědomí a na přístrojích, sdělili v pátek soudu její obhájci. data.title: Prezident Pavel nepůjde ke komunálním volbám. Zachytili jej na rallye v Maroku
data.description: Prezident Petr Pavel se kvůli soukromé zahraniční cestě za týden nezúčastní hlasování ve volbách do zastupitelstva obce Černouček na Litoměřicku. Na webu to oznámil odbor komunikace prezidentské kanceláře. Doplnil, že prezidenta chyba v plánování mrzí. Automobilový jezdec Martin Prokop dnes večer na svém facebooku napsal, že Petr Pavel navštívil rallye v Maroku, a zveřejnil fotografii s hlavou státu.

data.title: Na chybu v plánování má nárok i hlava státu. Kdo něco podobného nezažil, ať hodí kamenem
data.description: Znáte to, lístky na ten koncert jsem koupil své ženě, ale těšil jsem se hlavně já. Kdo by nechtěl vidět dirigovat a zpívat na Pražském jaru atraktivní Barbaru Hannigan. data.title: Pavlova dovolená o volbách? Macinka žertuje, Turek by zrušil i cestu na Měsíc
data.description: Rozhodnutí prezidenta Petra Pavla vynechat příští týden komunální volby v Černoučku kvůli soukromé cestě vyvolalo rozporuplné reakce. Například ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka prohlásil, že jej prezidentova neúčast velice mrzí, ale pokud by v Černoučku preferoval jinou volbu než Motoristy, přeje mu klidný odpočinek a přimlouvá se za to, aby vzal pár podobně politicky smýšlejících sousedů s sebou. Spolustraník Filip Turek pro krok prezidenta nemá pochopení.

data.title: Base das Lajes. BE diz que "inquérito desmonta todo o discurso do Governo"
data.description: O Ministério Público está a investigar a utilização norte-americana da Base das Lajes. O inquérito é "instaurado na sequência de uma denúncia apresentada por elementos do Bloco de Esquerda". O coordenador do Bloco, José Manuel Pureza, considera que é preciso esperar pelas conclusões do inquérito, mas entende que, “ao dar este passo”, o Ministério Público reconhece que “há fundamento” na queixa apresentada pelo partido.

data.title: How local can a global restaurant really be?
data.description: In hospitality, standardisation creates a sense of trust; in gastronomy, it can sometimes disconnect a restaurant from the place it inhabits. data.title: Élection historique à Hambourg : le Camerounais Maurice Kengne Kamga prend la tête du Tribunal international du droit de la mer
data.description: © DR Le Camerounais Maurice Kengne Kamga a été porté le 1er octobre 2026 à la tête du Tribunal International du Droit de la Mer (TIDM) pour un mandat de trois ans (2026-2029). Élu par ses pairs, il succède à l'Islandais Tomas Heidar et devient le premier Camerounais à diriger cette juridiction de l'ONU. L'Argentine Frida Maria Armas Pfirter est vice-présidente. Basé à Hambourg, le TIDM qui fête ses 30 ans, tranche les litiges sur les océans : zones économiques, pêche, navigation, ressources offshore. Un enjeu direct pour le Cameroun, ouvert sur le Golfe de Guinée. Né en 1967 à Bandjoun, Kamga est bachelier en 1986 au lycée de New-Bell à Douala, puis diplômé en droit public à Yaoundé (licence 1989, maîtrise 1990, DEA 1991). Il intègre l'IRIC où il soutient en 1994 un doctorat sous la direction du Pr Maurice Kamto, qui l'inspire dès ses débuts. Diplomate depuis 1994, il est, la même année, lauréat de la bourse Hamilton Shirley Amerasinghe de l'ONU, unique bourse mondiale pour se spécialiser en droit de la mer. Il part à Genève où il obtient un second doctorat en droit international public en 2003 sous Lucius Caflisch, avec une thèse de référence : Délimitation maritime sur la côte atlantique africaine. De retour comme conseiller juridique au ministère des Relations extérieures et enseignant à l'IRIC, il est nommé en 2008 juriste référendaire à la Cour Internationale de Justice à La Haye, premier Africain subsaharien à ce niveau. Il y restera 13 ans tout en publiant et enseignant. En 2017, il soutient son HDR à Paris Nanterre sous Alain Pellet. Élu juge au TIDM en août 2020, il prend fonction en octobre 2020. Non résident à Hambourg, il rentre poursuivre ses projets académiques et dirige depuis 2021 le HITAS à Douala. De New-Bell à la présidence d'un tribunal mondial, c’est un parcours d'excellence. Cet article Élection historique à Hambourg : le Camerounais Maurice Kengne Kamga prend la tête du Tribunal international du droit de la mer est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Né en 1967 à Bandjoun, Kamga est bachelier en 1986 au lycée de New-Bell à Douala, puis diplômé en droit public à Yaoundé (licence 1989, maîtrise 1990, DEA 1991). Il intègre l'IRIC où il soutient en 1994 un doctorat sous la direction du Pr Maurice Kamto, qui l'inspire dès ses débuts. Diplomate depuis 1994, il est, la même année, lauréat de la bourse Hamilton Shirley Amerasinghe de l'ONU, unique bourse mondiale pour se spécialiser en droit de la mer. Il part à Genève où il obtient un second doctorat en droit international public en 2003 sous Lucius Caflisch, avec une thèse de référence : Délimitation maritime sur la côte atlantique africaine. De retour comme conseiller juridique au ministère des Relations extérieures et enseignant à l'IRIC, il est nommé en 2008 juriste référendaire à la Cour Internationale de Justice à La Haye, premier Africain subsaharien à ce niveau. Il y restera 13 ans tout en publiant et enseignant. En 2017, il soutient son HDR à Paris Nanterre sous Alain Pellet. Élu juge au TIDM en août 2020, il prend fonction en octobre 2020. Non résident à Hambourg, il rentre poursuivre ses projets académiques et dirige depuis 2021 le HITAS à Douala. De New-Bell à la présidence d'un tribunal mondial, c’est un parcours d'excellence. data.title: ISAR 43 à Genève : le Cameroun mise sur la transparence ESG pour attirer les financements durables
data.description: © DR Présent à Genève du 30 septembre au 2 octobre 2026, le ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze défend la stratégie camerounaise à la 43e session de l'ISAR. Objectif : fiabiliser l'information financière et extra-financière pour rassurer les investisseurs et débloquer des fonds durables. Mieux informer pour mieux financer. C'est le pari du Cameroun à la 43e session du Groupe de travail intergouvernemental d'experts des normes comptables (ISAR), organisée par la CNUCED à Genève. Conduite par le Ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze, la délégation camerounaise plaide pour un renforcement de la qualité et de la fiabilité des informations produites par les entreprises et les administrations, sur leurs performances économiques, sociales et environnementales. Ces données, regroupées sous les critères ESG (environnementaux, sociaux et de gouvernance), sont devenues la boussole des bailleurs. Elles permettent d'identifier les risques, d'améliorer la transparence et de renforcer la confiance des investisseurs. En marge des sessions, Louis Paul Motaze a multiplié les rencontres bilatérales avec Pedro Manuel Moreno, Secrétaire général adjoint de la CNUCED, et Nan Li Collins, Directrice de la Division Investissement et Entreprises. Au menu : une nouvelle phase d'assistance technique pour le Cameroun. La CNUCED devrait accompagner des entreprises pilotes, assurer la formation des professionnels, appuyer le développement des systèmes de données et surtout intégrer progressivement le reporting de durabilité dans le cadre comptable OHADA. L'enjeu est financier. Avec une information plus fiable et transparente, Yaoundé espère faciliter la mobilisation de financements durables, verts et responsables, au service de sa stratégie de développement. Cet article ISAR 43 à Genève : le Cameroun mise sur la transparence ESG pour attirer les financements durables est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: CEMAC : un budget 2027 en baisse, l’alerte rouge sur les caisses
data.description: © DR Réunis à Brazzaville du 26 au 28 septembre 2026, les experts du Comité Inter-États ont bouclé le projet de budget 2027 de la Communauté. Arrêté à 82,2 milliards FCFA, en recul de 4,28%, il sera soumis au Conseil des Ministres ce 2 octobre 2026, sur fond de crise de trésorerie liée à la TCI. L'heure est à la rigueur à la CEMAC. Les travaux préparatoires à la 46e Session Ordinaire du Conseil des Ministres de l'UEAC, tenus en hybride à Brazzaville, ont accouché d'un budget 2027 resserré : 82 246 966 095 FCFA en ressources et emplois, en baisse de 4,28% par rapport à 2026. Le montage repose sur 61,35 milliards de ressources ordinaires, dont 50,30 milliards issus de la Taxe Communautaire d'Intégration (TCI) maintenue au même niveau, et 20,89 milliards de ressources extraordinaires. Au-delà des chiffres, les experts ont passé en revue les grands chantiers : état d'avancement du Plan Stratégique 2027-2030 (PACTE 2030) adossé au Budget-Programme, feuille de route contre Ebola, et Plan d'Action Stratégique de la CEBEVIRHA. Mais le point le plus sensible a été la situation financière. La note de la Commission CEMAC est alarmante : très faible mobilisation de la TCI et non-versement des arriérés par une majorité d'États membres. Une dégradation qui menace la continuité des services et le fonctionnement même des institutions. Face à l'urgence, les experts ont approuvé une note d'alerte solennelle à l'attention des ministres, les appelant à des mesures de sauvegarde immédiates. L'ensemble des dossiers est désormais sur la table du Conseil des Ministres, qui statue le 2 octobre 2026 lors de sa 46e session ordinaire. Cet article CEMAC : un budget 2027 en baisse, l’alerte rouge sur les caisses est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Coopération Cameroun-USA : 510 milliards FCFA pour muscler le système de santé
data.description: © DR Yaoundé et Washington scellent un nouvel accord de don. 400 millions de dollars américains et 450 millions de dollars camerounais seront mobilisés d'ici 2030 pour bâtir un système de santé résilient, dans une logique de co-financement historique. Le parapheur a de nouveau chauffé entre Yaoundé et Washington. Le 1er octobre 2026, le Ministre de l'Économie, Alamine Ousmane Mey, et la Chargée d'Affaires américaine, Brenda Soya, ont signé l'Accord de Don SOAG pour un système de santé résilient et durable. Ce SOAG est l'opérationnalisation du Mémorandum d'entente du 16 décembre 2025. Il sécurise le plan d'action sur cinq ans. Sur la période 2026-2030, les États-Unis s'engagent à mobiliser 400 millions de dollars, soit près de 240 milliards FCFA. Le Cameroun, dans une logique de coresponsabilité assumée, mettra sur la table jusqu'à 450 millions de dollars, soit environ 270 milliards FCFA. Au total, plus de 510 milliards FCFA pour amorcer la transition vers un financement endogène de la santé. L'enveloppe cible six priorités : renforcer la lutte contre VIH, tuberculose et paludisme ; consolider la sécurité sanitaire, la surveillance épidémiologique et les laboratoires ; améliorer les chaînes d'approvisionnement pharmaceutique et les systèmes de données ; réduire la mortalité maternelle, néonatale et infantile ; renforcer la performance des districts de santé ; et promouvoir l'approche « Une Seule Santé ». Ce nouvel appui s'ajoute à un engagement massif : depuis 20 ans, les États-Unis ont injecté plus de 1,1 milliard de dollars, soit 640 milliards FCFA, dans la santé camerounaise. Cet article Coopération Cameroun-USA : 510 milliards FCFA pour muscler le système de santé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Réforme foncière au Cameroun : Yaoundé valide les grands arbitrages
data.description: © DR Au terme de deux jours de débats intenses, la deuxième session de la Plateforme Multi-Acteurs de Concertation a bouclé ses travaux le 1er octobre 2026. Sécurisation des droits coutumiers, agence nationale du cadastre, digitalisation : les piliers de la future loi foncière sont posés. C'est le laboratoire de la terre camerounaise. Le 1er octobre 2026, le Ministre des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires Foncières, Henri Eyebe Ayissi, a clos la deuxième session de la Plateforme Multi-Acteurs de Concertation (PMAC). Ouverte le 30 septembre, la session a planché sur le diagnostic sans fard de la gouvernance foncière présenté par le Dr Samuel Nguifo, Assistant Technique du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durables (PVGFD). Les échanges ont été crus. Faut-il un cadastre polyvalent générateur de ressources à l'image du Maroc, du Mali ou du Nigeria ? Comment distinguer foncier urbain et rural ? Faut-il décréter un moratoire sur les attributions ? Doit-on donner la personnalité juridique aux chefferies traditionnelles, encadrer la notion explosive de peuples autochtones, et imposer une vraie coordination interministérielle ? Pour répondre, cinq groupes thématiques ont travaillé : administrations publiques, MINDCAF, secteur privé et ordres professionnels, communautés locales et peuples autochtones, femmes et jeunes. De leurs travaux sont sortis des arbitrages forts : création d'une Agence nationale du cadastre et de l'information foncière, création d'une unité de suivi dans chaque structure, renforcement de la MAETUR, de la SIC et de la MAGZI, et transmission obligatoire des désignations des parties prenantes au MINDCAF. Dans son discours de clôture, Henri Eyebe Ayissi a salué « le laboratoire par excellence de l'intelligence collective au service de la terre ». Il a fixé les piliers de la vision : sécurisation des droits fonciers coutumiers, participation des chefferies à la gestion du domaine national, optimisation économique du patrimoine, digitalisation intégrale du cadastre et des conservations, avec genre, décentralisation et climat en transversal. La suite s'articule en trois jalons : finalisation du Document de Politique Nationale, convocation de l'Équipe Interministérielle, et lancement des consultations interrégionales sur les textes d'application. Le Ministre a remercié la Banque Mondiale via le PVGFD, la FAO, la GIZ et l'ONU, ainsi que la société civile et les autorités traditionnelles, « gardiens sacrés de nos terres ». Cet article Réforme foncière au Cameroun : Yaoundé valide les grands arbitrages est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Bunia : entre informations et idées reçues, le défi de la sensibilisation au cancer du sein
data.description: Alors que le mois d’octobre est consacré à la sensibilisation au cancer du sein à travers le monde, de nombreuses voix appellent à un renforcement des actions de prévention et d’information dans la ville de Bunia. Certaines femmes du chef-lieu de l’Ituri reconnaissent encore manquer de connaissances sur cette maladie, ses facteurs de risque et les moyens de dépistage. Une situation qui pourrait retarder le diagnostic et la prise en charge des patientes, estiment les experts médicaux.

data.title: Ebola en Ituri : 24 décès à Mahagi, aucun nouveau cas depuis près de deux mois
data.description: Le territoire de Mahagi, en Ituri, a enregistré 24 décès parmi les 50 cas positifs d’Ebola recensés dans la province depuis la déclaration de l’épidémie par les autorités. Ce vendredi 2 octobre, les autorités sanitaires rapportent toutefois qu’aucun nouveau cas n’a été enregistré à Mahagi depuis près de deux mois. Elles attribuent cette évolution notamment à l’implication des autorités politico-militaires dans la riposte.

data.title: Baffour Awuah expected in court as EOCO moves to meet bail deadline
data.description:
Manhyia South Member of Parliament Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah is expected to be arraigned before a weekend court as the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) moves to meet the constitutional timelines governing his detention.

The MP is likely to appear before Specialised Court 2, which sits at Commercial Court 5 of the High Court Complex in Accra, although the specific court and time of the appearance had not been officially announced at the time of publication.

EOCO said it was working with the Office of the Attorney-General to bring the MP before a weekend court, citing the applicable constitutional timeframes and procedural requirements governing bail.

data.title: Madagascar–France : Jean-Marc Grosgurin prend ses fonctions dans un contexte diplomatique en mutation
data.description: Une nouvelle étape s'ouvre dans les relations entre Madagascar et la France. Jean-Marc Grosgurin est désormais officiellement installé comme ambassadeur de France dans la Grande Île. Le diplomate a présenté ses lettres de créance au colonel Michaël Randrianirina, président de la Refondation, le 30 septembre au palais d'État d'Iavoloha. Nommé par décret présidentiel le 7 août 2026, Jean-Marc Grosgurin succède à Arnaud Guillois, arrivé au terme de sa mission en juillet. Sa prise de fonctions (…) - Politique

data.title: Dictateurs africains pour les Nuls* : Mode d'emploi

data.title: Evénement : Le 14 octobre devient la « Fête de la Liberté »
data.description: Le gouvernement malgache ajoutera dès cette année une nouvelle célébration majeure à son calendrier républicain. Le 14 octobre, anniversaire de la proclamation de la République malgache en 1958, sera désormais célébré sous l'appellation « Fête de la Liberté », avec une importance nationale comparable à celle accordée au 26 juin, jour de l'Indépendance. L'initiative a été annoncée à Mahazoarivo. Pour cette première édition, les cérémonies nationales se dérouleront les 13 et 14 octobre 2026 (…) - Politique

data.title: Financements : le FMI valide le décaissement de 155 millions de dollars
data.description: Une bonne nouvelle pour Madagascar sur le front financier. Le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) a donné son feu vert, mercredi 30 septembre, au décaissement immédiat d'environ 155 millions de dollars en faveur du pays. Son Conseil d'administration a validé les troisième et quatrième revues combinées de la Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC) et de la Facilité pour la résilience et la durabilité (FRD). Les deux programmes, d'une durée de 36 mois, avaient été approuvés en juin 2024. La somme (…) - Economie

Hasta el momento, más de 1 000 institutos se han visto afectados por las manifestaciones, con bloqueos en 222 de ellos. data.title: Cuba avanza en la creación de una red de gastronomía ligera: ¿Qué establece la nueva resolución?
data.description: Cuba avanza hacia la creación de una red de gastronomía ligera para dinamizar este servicio, con la publicación hoy de la Resolución 29/2026 del Ministerio del Comercio Interior en la Gaceta Oficial. La norma establece las bases para puntos de venta móviles y fijos, con alimentos de fácil elaboración y consumo rápido, e incorpora incentivos para los actores económicos participantes. The post Cuba avanza en la creación de una red de gastronomía ligera: ¿Qué establece la nueva resolución? first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Cuba abrirá el próximo domingo la 65 Serie Nacional de Béisbol
data.description: Cuba abrirá su 65ª Serie Nacional de Béisbol el próximo domingo 4 de octubre con 16 equipos. El campeonato se efectuará con una división geográfica occidental y oriental, cada una con dos grupos de cuatro conjuntos, que disputarán 44 partidos por novena en la etapa de clasificación. El desafío inicial será entre los Cocodrilos de Matanzas y los Elefantes de Cienfuegos. The post Cuba abrirá el próximo domingo la 65 Serie Nacional de Béisbol first appeared on Cubadebate .

Si nada cambia, las futuras generaciones podrían no tener un mañana ni registros de nuestra época. No obstante, sí hay salida y es la presentada por el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, sostiene el periodista ruso Víctor Ternovsky en una nueva entrega de “Cuadernos de un moscovita”, una colaboración entre @Cubadebate y @SputnikMundo. The post Putin presenta la receta contra el abismo mundial first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: José Molina da la cara tras derrota de Honduras y explica los cambios en el 11 ante Martinica
data.description: La Selección Nacional de Honduras sufrió una dolorosa derrota 2-1 ante Martinica y quedó al borde de la eliminación en la Nations League 2026 . La Bicolor volvió a mostrar problemas para sostener el partido y terminó pagando caro sus errores en un encuentro donde tuvo oportunidades para conseguir un resultado diferente. Tras el pitazo final, el técnico José Francisco Molina habló en conferencia de prensa reconoció que Honduras tuvo opciones para marcar y destacó la mejoría del equipo en el segundo tiempo, aunque lamentó que las equivocaciones defensivas nuevamente fueran determinantes. El entrenador español también explicó los cambios realizados en el once titular y aseguró que el objetivo ahora es recuperarse y buscar la victoria ante Jamaica el próximo lunes 5 de octubre. Análisis tras el final del partido: Creo que en la primera parte nos costó un poco seguir la dinámica que veníamos teniendo de Jamaica, pero aun así tuvimos una primera parte en la que dominamos el juego. Tuvimos más ocasiones que Martinica, a pesar de que Martinica marcó un gol y tuvo un penalti, pero creo que nosotros tuvimos varias acciones muy buenas para marcar. Desgraciadamente, no estuvimos acertados. En la segunda parte los cambios nos vinieron bien en cuanto al juego. Mejoramos, tuvimos el balón, con más sentido y seguimos teniendo ocasiones, pero es verdad que el paso del tiempo se volvió quizás un poco de ida y vuelta, que es algo que no nos gusta, y ahí ellos aprovecharon una acción para marcar un gol. Nosotros también pudimos incluso empatar al final. La sensación es que los errores que cometemos nos cuestan muy caro. En todos los partidos en los que jugamos, cada vez que cometemos un error, el rival nos penaliza y eso, lógicamente, no es bueno. Sobre los cambios en el 11 titular: No creo que fuera excesivo. Si lo miras del último partido, tú piensas en seis cambios, pero había jugadores que habían jugado el último partido, aunque no fuera de inicio. Había jugadores que habían jugado el primer partido y no el segundo. Era un poco refrescar el equipo. Veníamos con ya dos partidos con algunos jugadores que habían jugado muchos minutos, demasiados, y teníamos que darles un poco de respiro. Con otros no lo hicimos porque no queríamos hacer tantos cambios. Y, al final, a esos que no cambiamos les noto ya más cansados. Lógicamente, sí. Pienso en analizar este partido más detenidamente para sacar mejores conclusiones y, a partir de ahí, pensar en el próximo partido contra Jamaica para volver a trabajar y volver a enfrentarlo con las mismas ganas, con la misma ilusión que hemos enfrentado este, de intentar hacer un buen partido, de ganarlo. Desgraciadamente, hoy no lo pudimos hacer, pero esperamos poder hacerlo el próximo. Lo que rescata de esta derrota: El objetivo es que estábamos teniendo el balón, pero nos costaba mucho cuando lo perdíamos. Ellos nos estaban cogiendo la espalda de los dos mediocentros con demasiada facilidad. Hablé con ellos para intentar solucionar eso. Creo que Kervin es un jugador que tiene calidad para tener el balón, tiene mucho recorrido. Deiby también andaba ya más desgastado. El ingreso de Kervin Arriaga: La intención seguía siendo la misma: seguir teniendo el balón con sentido, pero tener un hombre con más recorrido. data.translatedTitle: José Molina da la cara tras derrota de Honduras y explica los cambios en el 11 ante Martinica

La Bicolor volvió a mostrar problemas para sostener el partido y terminó pagando caro sus errores en un encuentro donde tuvo oportunidades para conseguir un resultado diferente. Tras el pitazo final, el técnico José Francisco Molina habló en conferencia de prensa reconoció que Honduras tuvo opciones para marcar y destacó la mejoría del equipo en el segundo tiempo, aunque lamentó que las equivocaciones defensivas nuevamente fueran determinantes. data.title: Lo que ocupa Honduras para clasificar a cuartos de final de la Concacaf Nations League
data.description: Honduras tropezó en el momento más complicado de la Concacaf Nations League tras perder ante Martinica por la tercera fecha . Esta derrota complica todo el panorama de la Bicolor en el cierre del torneo que los llevará a los cuartos de final y a la Copa Oro 2027 . La 'H' comparte el Grupo B de la Liga A de la Nations League con Jamaica , Surinam , Guatemala , Martinica y El Salvador . De acuerdo con el reglamento de Concacaf , los dos primeros lugares de cada grupo avanzarán a los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones, donde se enfrentarán a los cuatro equipos (México, Estados Unidos, Canadá y Panamá) mejor clasificados de la región que ya tienen asegurado su lugar en esa instancia. La derrota ante Martinica representa un retroceso para Honduras , pero todavía tendrá que disputar un partido restante de la fase de grupos. Luego de perder, la 'H' ya no depende de sí misma y eso es lo peor de todo. Honduras se quedó con tres puntos, mismos que El Salvador , selección que está enfrentando ahora a Jamaica (3 pts). Surinam tiene 7 puntos y Martinica sumó sus primeros puntos y se mete a la pelea. Ahora la 'H' tendrá que ir a ganarle obligatoriamente a Jamaica el lunes 5 de octubre, pero tendrá que esperar resultados de los otros rivales. Si Honduras gana llegaría a seis unidades y tendrá que esperar que Guatemala pierda ante Surinam. Igual hoy Honduras necesita que Jamaica y El Salvador empaten para que no se alejen. Ahora la Bicolor deberá de esperar de otras selecciones y también a pelear el descenso a la Liga B. ¿Qué pasa si Honduras termina primero o segundo? Si Honduras termina entre los dos primeros lugares del Grupo B, avanzará a los cuartos de final de la Nations League . Esa ronda se disputará a partidos de ida y vuelta durante noviembre de 2026. Los cuatro ganadores de las series avanzarán a las Finales de la Liga A y obtendrán automáticamente su clasificación a la Copa Oro 2027 . Pero incluso si la Bicolor consigue avanzar a cuartos de final y posteriormente pierde su serie, todavía tendrá una oportunidad de llegar al máximo torneo de selecciones de Concacaf . Los cuatro equipos derrotados en los cuartos de final tendrán acceso a los Prelims de la Copa Oro 2027. ¿Qué pasa si termina tercero o cuarto? Si Honduras no logra terminar entre los dos primeros de su grupo, pero finaliza tercero o cuarto, avanzará directamente a los Prelims de la Copa Oro 2027. Es decir, todavía conservaría una vía para buscar su clasificación al torneo. Los Prelims serán una instancia de eliminación en la que las selecciones deberán superar su respectiva serie para conseguir el boleto a la Copa Oro. Por eso, incluso quedar fuera de los cuartos de final no significaría automáticamente el adiós para la Bicolor. ¿Y si Honduras termina quinto o sexto? El panorama sería más complicado, pero tampoco significaría la eliminación. Los equipos que terminen quinto y sexto en los grupos de la Liga A avanzarán al Play-In de la Nations League. En esa instancia participarán los cuatro equipos de la Liga A que terminen en quinto y sexto lugar, además de los tres ganadores de grupo y el mejor segundo lugar de la Liga C. Los cuatro ganadores de las series de ida y vuelta avanzarán a los Prelims de la Copa Oro 2027. Por lo tanto, Honduras todavía tendría una ruta hacia la Copa Oro incluso si termina en la parte baja de su grupo, aunque necesitaría superar más obstáculos para conseguir el boleto.
